shared_elements: bird with hooked/pointed beak shown in profile
horizontal band of repeated marks along the top edge
raised bosses/discs (top of A, curls and mounts in B)
justification: Both are stone reliefs dominated by a profile bird-headed creature with extended wing-like limbs, and both carry a narrow band of repeated marks running along the upper edge, which is the most specific correspondence. However A is a tall pillar with several small, shallow, schematic figures stacked in loose registers, while B is a single rectangular slab filled by one large, deeply modelled figure with meticulous feather striations and spiral curls — the carving depth, scale and compositional logic are quite different.
